headline: All majors above the 200-day line with overbought momentum, but whales rotating into exchanges and funding at 11% annual while BTC treads water on the day.
paragraphs: The entire major asset roster sits above its 200-day moving average: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all in uptrend by that measure. No golden crosses are lit, meaning the 50-day has not yet reclaimed the 200-day, so the longer-term regime is rising but the intermediate structure has not fully reset. The contradiction is not a weakness, it is the normal rhythm of a recovery move: prices have traveled a long way from their 12-month lows (Bitcoin down 37.9% from the 124,740 high, Ethereum down 49.3% from 4,818, Solana down 61.9% from 248), yet the bars have moved fast enough to get ahead of their own averages. MACD is above signal across all seven: momentum is positive. The test now is whether that momentum can hold or whether the overbought RSI readings (Bitcoin 81.9, Ethereum 79.8, Solana 83.5, XRP 87.1, BNB 83.9, Doge 82.7, Cardano 77.8) are the market's way of signaling fatigue after seven to thirty days of gains.

On the day, the story is mixed: Bitcoin and Ethereum both fell on the 24-hour print (down 1.12% and 2.96%, respectively), but over the seven-day window both have climbed sharply (Bitcoin up 22.13%, Ethereum up 29.98%). Over the month, gains persist (Bitcoin 20.79%, Ethereum 35.95%, XRP 39.13%, Cardano 39.34%). The intraday weakness sits inside a multi-week strength, which is a classic behavior of a position that has run hard and is now consolidating. Fear and Greed stands at 71, in the greed zone after a 30-day range of 25 to 72, suggesting the crowd is at the upper end of its sentiment band but not at an extreme.

Leverage markets show funding at 0.01% per 8-hour period, or 11% annualized across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and DOGE on OKX. That rate is neither cheap nor severe, it is the normal cost of holding leverage in a rising market. Open interest is substantial: BTC at 2.24 billion, ETH at 1.37 billion, SOL at 265 million. Long-to-short ratios are tilted toward longs (BTC 1.14, ETH 1.21, SOL 2.15, XRP 1.62, DOGE 3.43), with Doge showing the most extreme skew. Liquidations over recent windows show a persistent bias toward long casualties: in the last 8 hours for Bitcoin, 14.88 million long USD was liquidated versus 3.39 million short; for Ethereum over the last hour, 20.22 million long to 3.88 million short. This pattern repeats across all symbols. The message is simple: leverage is present, it is expensive to hold, and it is currently being shaken out on the long side.

Whale flows over the last 24 hours show 160.26 million dollars moving onto exchanges, a reversal from the prior two weeks where coins were fleeing (Aug 1 and Aug 8 saw 922 million and 484 million move off exchanges). The flow into exchanges comes almost entirely from Ethereum inflows of 161.64 million, while Bitcoin saw a small net outflow of 1.38 million. More striking is the composition of the largest moves: 1.5 billion in Tether moved onto Binance and Bitfinex, while 900 million in Tether moved off Binance. This looks like position squaring and liquidity chasing rather than a panic or a capitulation. Stablecoin float stands at 308.5 billion, virtually flat on the month (up 0.27%), so dry powder has not accumulated; it is simply being shuffled between venues and wallets.

ETF spot flows remain decisively positive: Bitcoin took in 307.5 million on August 21 and has maintained inflows for all five consecutive sessions, with a cumulative five-session net of 1.92 billion and a lifetime cumulative of 53.78 billion. Ethereum took in 184 million on August 21 and has also persisted at inflows for five days straight, cumulative five-session net of 693 million and lifetime of 12.15 billion. Traditional finance is still buying, which stands in contrast to the whale reshuffling and the overbought technicals. This is a structural bid beneath the rally.

Watch for three things: whether the overbought RSI readings begin to curl lower without a fresh price breakdown (a momentum divergence that would signal fatigue), whether the long liquidations accelerate if price touches support (a sign that leverage is too hot), and whether the flow of coins back onto exchanges continues or reverses (a tell on whether the institutional bid is holding or whether whales are front-running a shift). The tape currently reads as a well-fed rally with some froth on top, supported from below by ETF buyers and underpinned by rising fundamentals (Bitcoin dominance at 58.7%, total market cap 2.64 trillion), but also showing signs that the move may need to rest.
